reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker or PD data reported to confirm lirilumab engaged KIR2DL1/2/3 or that nivolumab/azacitidine engaged their targets. Target engagement cannot be assessed. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers reported to confirm NK cell activation or epigenetic reprogramming occurred. Pathway modulation cannot be assessed. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint (ORR) was not met. Overall effect size was 7/10 participants with response, but this appears to be across all arms. Individual arm outcomes show partial responses only - low/intermediate-1 MDS group had 1 response, high-risk MDS group had 6 responses. Without historical benchmarks or controls, these modest response rates suggest limited clinical benefit. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. Cannot assess differential responses. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Trial was terminated early due to sponsor's commercial decision not to pursue lirilumab in myeloid malignancies. Small sample size (n=10) across multiple arms. High toxicity burden with 50% febrile neutropenia in the azacitidine combination arm and multiple serious adverse events. The early termination for commercial reasons combined with the modest efficacy signals and high toxicity suggests this was primarily a commercial decision rather than a pure efficacy failure.

failure_modes.evidence: Trial was terminated early due to sponsor's decision not to pursue lirilumab development in myeloid malignancies, not due to futility or safety concerns alone
Very small sample size of 10 patients across multiple arms prevents meaningful efficacy assessment

edges_to_update.reasoning: Lirilumab monotherapy arm showed minimal response (1/2 patients), suggesting NK cell receptor antagonism did not effectively drive anti-tumor immunity
Combination arm with azacitidine showed partial responses but trial was terminated early, suggesting limited efficacy of NK cell mechanism
Azacitidine combination showed only partial responses and trial was terminated, suggesting epigenetic reprogramming mechanism had limited efficacy
NK cell mediated anti-tumor immunity did not translate to meaningful clinical responses in MDS
Epigenetic reprogramming did not drive sufficient clinical benefit in high-risk MDS
ORR is an appropriate endpoint for MDS and was measured, though responses were limited
Limited responses across different MDS risk groups suggest this population did not respond well to the interventions

review_reason: Trial terminated early for commercial reasons with very small sample size makes it difficult to assess true mechanistic failure vs operational issues
